implementation_notes: Ruby's stdlib has no monads, so the pattern is hand-written or taken from the dry-monads gem: Result (Success/Failure) and Maybe (Some/None) provide bind/fmap, and including Dry::Monads[:result, :do] turns yield into bind, so a pipeline reads as straight-line code with one error track (railway-oriented programming). Use it where failures must be values with a reason; otherwise raise/rescue plus &. already express the common cases with less machinery.
code_sketch:
include Dry::Monads[:result, :do]

def call(user_id)
  user   = yield find_user(user_id)   # Failure short-circuits the block
  orders = yield orders_of(user)      # depends on the previous value
  Success(summarize(user, orders))
end
pitfalls: do-notation requires including the :do slice as well as the monad slices; a bare yield then raises at runtime, not at load time.
Mixing Maybe and Result forces conversions (to_result/fmap) and loses the reason for absence; keep one track per pipeline.
A raise inside a bind block still aborts with an exception - the monad tracks values, not exceptions.

variants.name: Safe navigation (&.) + Object#then pipelines
variants.implementation_notes: For the Maybe case the local idiom is &. (call only when the receiver is not nil, else nil) combined with Object#then (Ruby 2.6, the renamed yield_self) to keep the pipeline shape, which covers chained optional lookups without a container class. It is a weaker structure than a monad - the result is nil rather than a typed absence and there is no bind for a step - so reach for dry-monads when the difference between 'missing' and 'failed' matters.
variants.code_sketch:
city_name = user&.address&.city&.name    # nil short-circuits the chain

report = params[:id]
  .then { |id| users.find(id) }          # keeps a pipeline shape
  .then { |user| user && summarize(user) }
pitfalls: &. collapses every failure mode into one nil, so callers cannot distinguish 'not found' from 'not permitted'.
A nil produced mid-chain is easy to miss: the NoMethodError simply disappears instead of being handled.
